output.summary: KEP-3107 adds a secretRef field to the CSI PersistentVolume source so kubelet can pass per-PVC secrets to CSI drivers in the NodeExpandVolume request. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: CSI drivers had no way to use a secret during node-side operations, because the NodeExpandVolume request carried no credentials, while the controller-side ControllerExpandVolume already had a secretRef. The KEP adds NodeExpandSecretRef to CSIPersistentVolumeSource so the request can carry per-PVC secrets. The alternative of drivers storing secrets elsewhere in the cluster was judged hacky by the authors.

alternatives.option: CSI drivers store the secrets somewhere in the cluster and read them during node expansion
alternatives.why_not: The KEP calls this a really hacky way and says CSI driver authors do not want it.

alternatives.option: Also add secretRef to other CSI calls such as NodeStageVolume
alternatives.why_not: These are explicit non-goals; the secretRef is limited to the NodeExpandVolume operation.

evidence.quote: Currently, the CSI drivers dont have a method to make use of secretRef at time of Node operation (ex: nodeExpansion) as the subjected csi request does not carry a secret or credentials in the request.
Other CSI calls e.g. `NodeStageVolume` will not have the secretRef in the request, this is limited to `NodeExpandVolume` operation.

Instead of fetching secretRef from the nodeExpansion request, CSI drivers can store those somewhere in the cluster and make use of it while doing nodeExpansion, however this is really a hacky way and not the CSI driver authors want.
